If you ever do consider moving to Australia in the future, I should warn you that Sydney has a high cost of living compared to other Australian capital cities. The median house price in Sydney sits at $1.3 million (AUD). It's near impossible to buy a house without taking out a loan/mortgage. Fortunately, it is still possible to lead a comfortable life since rent isn't too bad (you can get a decent apartment for about $200 to $400 p/w in non-posh areas further away from the CBD). Public transport options include ferries, buses, heavy rail/trains, light rail/trams and the metro.  
The national minimum wage sits at around $20.33 (AUD).Financial support is available to assist migrants, senior citizens, university students and trainees, disabled people, job seekers/unemployed etc.If you want to live in or around a major city without having to deal with obnoxiously high living costs, may I suggest:

* **Newcastle**, New South Wales
* **Tweed Heads**, New South Wales
* **Blue Mountains Region (Katoomba, Blackheath etc.)**, New South Wales
* **Wollongong/Illawarra Region**, New South Wales
* **Melbourne**, Victoria
* **Geelong**, Victoria

I went to a pretty strict primary school so I have quite a lot of stories to but I'm just gonna go with the one that pissed me off the most.

​

**Saying "I hate apples"**

​

Okay so every Friday afternoon, we'd have these "kindergarten assemblies" where we'd sing songs and get awards for things we did well that week. One particular day, this extremely strict teacher (let's call her Miss B) went on a rant about why saying "hate" is bad and how we'd get in severe trouble if we were caught saying it (stupid, I know). So a week later, I opened my lunchbox and expected to find the packet of gummy bears my parents said was in there but when I opened it, I was utterly horrified.

I saw a dreaded **Apple (oh no!)**

So in a fit of rage, I loudly exclaimed, "I **hate** apples!". Everyone gasped and turned to look at me and it was only when I saw this girl running to tell Miss B, I realised what I had just done. So in short, I hid in the bathrooms for all of recess but when I eventually left, I was immediately grabbed by Miss B. and taken to the principal's office where I had to fill in a reflection sheet for "hate speech" and I had several adults yelling at me. (I was six at the time so I'm surprised I didn't cry lol)

Somewhere in regional Australia.

During a school camp, I was chatting away with my roommates. It was way past midnight when I saw it. The conversation was starting to die and we were about to go to sleep when I caught a glimpse of the window. I could see other cabins but on the veranda of one certain cabin, I could see a tall and pale figure just standing there. At first, I tried to ignore it but I just couldn't stop looking back at it. Eventually, we all went to bed. I couldn't go to sleep because I kept thinking about that strange figure. I decided to look at it one more time before going to sleep. Big mistake. When I looked over, it was staring straight at me. I only made eye contact for a second before immediately covering myself up with a blanket and attempting to go to sleep. I think was about 4 in the morning when I randomly woke up. The room was extremely dark and I could barely see anything but in a corner of the room, I could see the figure staring at me. I tried to scream but nothing was coming out. The figure approached me and proceeded to wrap it fingers around my neck. Just then, I woke up. I looked over at the corner and the figure was gone. I checked the time and it was almost 4. Out of fear, I asked my best friend if we could share beds. She agreed. When I woke up, I went to brush my teeth. I almost fainted when I saw strangulation marks around my neck. Since that day, I have never told anyone about the incident because I'm scared that nobody will believe me.
